transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I guess the main thing is my sleep. It’s been going on for a long time, and I just feel worn down by it. I’ll be exhausted by the end of the day, like I can barely keep myself moving, and then I fall into bed thinking I should just sleep straight through—but I don’t. I wake up over and over, sometimes from the tiniest sounds in the house, things I feel like other people would sleep right through.

And then I’m awake before the alarm, just lying there, already tired before the day even starts. It’s that feeling like I was in bed for hours but didn’t actually rest, if that makes sense. I’m here because I don’t feel like I can keep brushing it off as just being tired anymore.
When you get into bed at night, how long does it usually take you to fall asleep?

Usually I fall asleep pretty fast, honestly, because by the time I get into bed I’m just wiped out. It’s not so much lying there for hours trying to fall asleep at the beginning. I kind of collapse into bed exhausted.

The problem is that it doesn’t stay asleep, if that makes sense. I’ll wake up again and again, sometimes from the smallest noises in the house—like little sounds that I feel like other people wouldn’t even notice. And then I’m often awake before the alarm, just lying there feeling like I never really got real rest, even though I was technically in bed.
Do you often wake up feeling as though you haven’t rested at all, even after a full night in bed?

Yes. That’s actually one of the most frustrating parts of it. I can be in bed for what should be a full night, and technically I slept some, but I wake up feeling like I didn’t get real rest at all.

It’s like my sleep is so broken up that it doesn’t count. I’ll fall into bed already exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house, even tiny things, and it happens enough that by the time morning comes, I’m already awake before the alarm. I just lie there feeling worn out before I’ve even started the day, like my body never really settled down.
During the day, do you often feel sleepy or struggle to stay awake, even after a full night in bed?

Yes, I do. I mean, it’s not always like I’m literally nodding off where I’m sitting, but I feel worn down during the day, like I’m dragging myself through it. That’s part of why I came in, because it’s been going on for a long time and I can’t really pretend it’s just a bad night here and there.

I’ll go to bed completely exhausted, thinking, okay, surely I’ll sleep, and then I wake up to every little sound in the house. It’s like my sleep breaks into pieces. Then I’m awake before the alarm, just lying there, and when I get up I already feel like I never really rested. So by daytime, even if I was in bed long enough, I don’t feel refreshed. I feel like I’m starting the day already behind.
Do you ever feel like even when you do sleep, it’s not refreshing or restful, like your body didn’t really get the chance to recover?

Yes, exactly. That’s honestly a big part of why I’m here. It’s been going on for a long time now where I’ll get into bed already exhausted, like my body should just shut down and recover, but the sleep I do get feels broken up.

I wake up to every little sound in the house — things that probably shouldn’t even wake me — and it’s like I never sink into that deep, restful kind of sleep. Then I’m up before the alarm, just lying there, already tired, feeling like the night didn’t really do anything for me. So even if I was technically in bed for enough hours, it doesn’t feel like my body actually got a chance to rest.
Do you often wake up feeling as though you didn’t sleep at all, even if you were in bed for a long time?

Yes, very often. I know I’ve already said it a few ways, but that’s really what keeps happening. I can be in bed for a long stretch, like long enough that you’d think I should feel at least somewhat rested, but when I wake up it feels like I barely slept at all.

I fall into bed exhausted, and then instead of getting real sleep, I’m waking up to every little sound in the house. It’s like my body never fully lets go. And then I’m usually awake before the alarm, just lying there, already tired, thinking, how am I supposed to get through the day if I’m starting out feeling like this? So yes, even after being in bed a long time, I wake up feeling like I never really rested.
Can you describe what your sleep feels like during the night—do you feel like you’re going through cycles of deep and light sleep, or does it feel more like you’re barely sleeping at all?

It feels more like I’m barely sleeping, honestly. I don’t really have a sense of, you know, going down into deep sleep and then coming back up in a normal way. It’s more like I fall into bed completely exhausted, and I think I must be asleep at some points, but it feels so broken up that it doesn’t count the way it should.

I wake up to every little sound in the house — like things I don’t think should be enough to wake a person — and then I’m aware of the room, aware of the time, trying to get comfortable again. Then maybe I drift off, maybe I don’t, but it never feels like I’ve really settled into anything restful.

And then I’m awake before the alarm, just lying there, already tired. So when morning comes, it doesn’t feel like I went through a real night of sleep. It feels like I spent hours in bed, but my body never actually got the rest it needed.
Even when you’re able to sleep without waking up, do you still wake up feeling like you didn’t get restful sleep?

Yeah… I mean, it’s hard for me to separate it out sometimes, because most nights I am waking up. That’s kind of the pattern — I fall into bed already exhausted, and then every little sound in the house seems to pull me back awake. But even on nights where I think maybe I slept more straight through, I still don’t wake up feeling restored.

It’s like being in bed doesn’t translate into actually resting. I’ll open my eyes before the alarm and just feel tired right away, like my body never got into that deeper kind of sleep. So yes, even if I don’t remember waking up as much, I still wake up with that same feeling that I didn’t really recover overnight.
Even if you sleep through the night without waking up, do you still wake up feeling unrefreshed or like you haven’t truly rested?

Yes… yes, that’s exactly it. Even if I don’t remember waking up over and over, I still wake up feeling like I haven’t truly rested. It’s like my body was in the bed all night, but it didn’t actually get sleep in the way it’s supposed to.

Most of the time it is broken up — I fall into bed exhausted, and then every little sound in the house wakes me, and I’m kind of in and out all night. But even on a “better” night, if you can call it that, I’m still up before the alarm feeling tired already. Not just sleepy like, oh, I need coffee, but more like I never really got restored in the first place. It’s been going on long enough that I almost expect to wake up that way now.
Even when you have slept for a long time without waking up, do you still wake up feeling like you haven’t truly rested, as if your sleep wasn’t restorative?

Yes… even if I’ve been in bed for a long time, and even if I don’t remember being awake as much, I still get up feeling like I didn’t really rest. That’s honestly a big part of why I’m here, because this has been going on for so long now.

Most nights it feels broken anyway — I fall into bed just completely worn out, and then it’s like every little sound in the house wakes me up. Something creaks, someone moves around, a car outside, anything, and I’m awake again. Then I’m lying there trying to tell myself to go back to sleep, checking the time even though I know that makes it worse.

But even on nights where I think, “Well, maybe I slept longer that time,” I’m still up before the alarm, already tired. It doesn’t feel restorative. It feels like my body was lying there all night, but I never got that deep, real rest that people talk about.
Even when you have slept for a long time without waking up, do you still wake up feeling like you haven’t truly rested, as if your sleep wasn’t restorative?

Yes, I do. I know I’ve probably said it a few different ways, but that’s really one of the main reasons I’m here. For a long time now, my sleep just hasn’t felt like real sleep.

I’ll go to bed already exhausted, like I’m completely drained, and you’d think that would mean I’d sleep hard, but it doesn’t work that way. Most nights it feels broken up. I wake up to every little sound in the house — a floorboard, a door, something outside — and once I’m awake, even if it’s only for a minute, it feels like I never fully settle back in.

And even on the nights where I’m in bed for a long stretch and I don’t remember waking up as much, I’m still awake before the alarm feeling tired right away. Not just “I don’t want to get up,” but more like my body never got the kind of rest it was supposed to get. It’s like I was lying there all night, but I didn’t really recover.
Even when you have slept for a long time and haven’t woken up during the night, do you still wake up feeling as though your sleep wasn’t restorative, like your body didn’t truly recover?

Yes… yes, that’s exactly how it feels. Even if I’m in bed for a long time, it doesn’t feel like my body actually recovered. I’ll wake up before the alarm and already feel worn out, like I’m starting the day behind before I’ve even gotten up.

And most nights it isn’t even one long stretch anyway. I fall into bed exhausted, thinking I should just be out cold, but then every little sound in the house wakes me up. A door, a creak, something outside — it doesn’t take much. So even if I technically spent enough hours in bed, it doesn’t feel like real rest. It’s been like that for a long time now, and honestly that’s part of why I’m here.
